### `TimeFilter`

```python
class TimeFilter: ...
```

Dataclass.

Select a calendar day, an open time bound, or a closed time range.

Args:
    on: Whole calendar date, exclusive with start/end; datetimes are not accepted.
    start: Optional inclusive date or datetime boundary. A date means naive midnight.
    end: Optional inclusive datetime or whole-date endpoint. A date is represented
        by exclusive midnight of the next day.

Raises:
    TypeError: If selectors have unsupported types.
    ValueError: If no selector is supplied, on conflicts with bounds, bounds are
        reversed or have incompatible timezone awareness, or a date endpoint overflows.

At least one selector is required. Naive boundaries use Spark's session-timezone
interpretation when converted into timestamp predicates.

#### Methods

##### `record_status`

```python
record_status(*, dataset: str, layer: str, batch_id: str, job_run_id: int | str | None=None, job_name: str | None=None, job_id: int | str | None=None, job_trigger_type: str | None=None, job_context: Any=None) -> None
```

Append one successful dataset-operation record to the Delta table.

The method assigns ``completed_at`` with Spark's current timestamp
before appending the row; it does not rely on a table-column default.

Args:
    dataset: Unique logical dataset name.
    layer: Standardization, curation, or integration layer.
    batch_id: Dataset-specific logical batch identifier.
    job_run_id: Optional Databricks job run identifier.
    job_name: Optional Databricks job name.
    job_id: Optional Databricks job identifier.
    job_trigger_type: Optional Databricks ``job.trigger.type`` value.
    job_context: Optional JSON-compatible diagnostic context.

Raises:
    TypeError: If an argument has an invalid type or ``job_context``
        cannot be serialized to JSON.
    ValueError: If a required value is blank, an enum or identifier is
        invalid, JSON contains a non-finite number, or the configured
        schema is missing ``completed_at``.

Spark and Delta write failures propagate to the caller unchanged.

##### `find_statuses`

```python
find_statuses(*, latest_only: bool=True, dataset: str | RegexFilter | None=None, layer: str | RegexFilter | None=None, batch_id: str | RegexFilter | None=None, job_run_id: int | str | None=None, job_name: str | RegexFilter | None=None, job_id: int | str | None=None, job_trigger_type: str | RegexFilter | None=None, completed_at: TimeFilter | None=None) -> DataFrame
```

Return successful operation records matching the supplied filters.

Plain text values use exact equality. :class:`RegexFilter` values use
case-insensitive Spark ``rlike`` matching. Numeric job identifiers use
equality, and :class:`TimeFilter` selects a day or timestamp bounds.

All field filters are optional and are combined with logical AND. By
default, the lazy result contains only the newest match. Set
``latest_only=False`` to return every match ordered by ``completed_at``
newest first. Every table column is preserved. Spark and table-read
failures propagate unchanged.

Args:
    latest_only: Return at most one row when True (default).
    dataset: Optional exact dataset text or regex.
    layer: Optional supported layer or regex; exact values are uppercased.
    batch_id: Optional exact batch text or regex.
    job_run_id: Optional integer/numeric-string run ID; blank means no filter.
    job_name: Optional exact workflow name or regex.
    job_id: Optional integer/numeric-string job ID; blank means no filter.
    job_trigger_type: Optional exact trigger text or regex.
    completed_at: Optional TimeFilter for completion timestamps.

Returns:
    A lazy DataFrame. Latest-only ties use descending job_run_id with nulls last.

Raises:
    TypeError: If flags or filters have unsupported types.
    ValueError: If text is blank, an exact layer is unsupported, or an ID is invalid.

##### `find_latest_status`

```python
find_latest_status(*, dataset: str | RegexFilter | None=None, layer: str | RegexFilter | None=None, batch_id: str | RegexFilter | None=None, job_run_id: int | str | None=None, job_name: str | RegexFilter | None=None, job_id: int | str | None=None, job_trigger_type: str | RegexFilter | None=None, completed_at: TimeFilter | None=None) -> OperationStatusRecord | None
```

Return the newest matching successful operation, or ``None``.

Unlike :meth:`find_statuses`, this convenience method is eager. It
delegates all filtering and ordering to that method, then executes a
Spark action to retrieve the first row. Validation, table-read, regex,
and Spark failures propagate unchanged.

Args:
    dataset: Optional exact dataset text or RegexFilter.
    layer: Optional supported processing layer or RegexFilter.
    batch_id: Optional exact batch text or RegexFilter.
    job_run_id: Optional integer or numeric-string run ID.
    job_name: Optional exact job name or RegexFilter.
    job_id: Optional integer or numeric-string job ID.
    job_trigger_type: Optional exact trigger text or RegexFilter.
    completed_at: Optional TimeFilter for completion timestamps.

Returns:
    The newest record, breaking ties by descending job_run_id, or None.

Raises:
    TypeError: If a filter has an unsupported type.
    ValueError: If filter text, layer, or identifier values are invalid.

##### `resolve_dependency`

```python
resolve_dependency(criteria: Mapping[str, Any]) -> OperationStatusRecord | None
```

Return the newest successful record matching dependency criteria.

Args:
    criteria: find_latest_status filters with required non-null dataset and layer.

Returns:
    The newest matching record, or None when no upstream completion matches.

Raises:
    TypeError: If criteria or a filter has an invalid type.
    ValueError: If criteria is empty, includes unknown keys, lacks identity fields,
        or contains an invalid filter.

Executes a Spark lookup immediately; table and evaluation failures propagate.
